image_description: A side-profile view of a Rock Beauty (Holocanthus tricolor) swimming near coral formations. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and head, transitioning to a golden-yellow posterior body and tail. The background consists of textured brain coral and reef structures in blue-green water.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is visible but appears as a simple dark line or slit; the specific 'protrusible' structure and 'brush-like teeth' texture are not resolved or clearly depicted.
The eye is prominent, large relative to the head, and clearly defined with a pupil and iris.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed disc-shaped body with compact proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish exhibits the correct high-bodied, laterally compressed profile typical of angelfish/butterflyfish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Striking gold and black coloration: anterior body and head black, posterior body and tail golden yellow with black margin.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The color pattern matches the taxonomy perfectly: black front half, yellow back half. A faint dark margin is visible on the tail edge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Continuous dorsal fin with spiny anterior and soft-rayed posterior portions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin runs continuously along the back. While individual rays aren't distinct due to resolution, the continuous structure is present.
The anal fin is visible on the ventral side, mirroring the shape of the posterior dorsal fin.
The caudal fin (tail) has a distinctly rounded, fan-like shape.
